text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- German Finance Minister Theo Waigel, on a brief visit to Austria, said on Sunday Germany would fulfil the Maastricht convergence criteria "without ifs and buts".
Austrian Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger said Austria would meet the criteria for a single currency without needing another austerity budget.
- Social Democrats suffer bigger-than-expected setback in the Klagenfurt mayoral elections, while the conservative People's Party's candidate won through with 67.8 percent of votes.
- 200 Austrians were cut off from the rest of the country on Sunday after a rock slide in the western province of Salzburg made roads impassable.
- Paper factory Steyrermuehl, taken over last year by Germany's Haindl-Papier, nearly doubled its earnings in 1996 to some 400 million schillings.
- London-based credit rating agency IBCA raised the long-term rating of bank Creditanstalt CABV_pa.vi to AA- from A+ and the short-term rating to A1+ from A1.
- Current affairs magazine Profil said national grid company Verbund has protested to Economics Minister Johann Farnleitner over his plans for the energy restructuring law.
- The president of Austria's construction industry, Horst Poechhacker, expects a drastic increase in joblessness in the building industry due to a caving in of housebuilding.
- Finance Minister Edlinger aims to reduce Austria's total debts to 66-67 percent of gross domestic product this year from above 70 percent in order to fulfil the Maastricht criteria.
- Economics Minister Farnleitner of the conservative People's Party rejects Transport Minister and Social Democrat Caspar Einem's proposal for a new telecommunications law.
- The NATO summit in Madrid in July will offer Austria entry into the alliance.
- The Hungarian subsidiaries of brewery Brau-Union, Sopron and Martfu, have substantially raised their earnings last year and now plan to pay a dividend of 15 percent.
